Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১) A dishonest milkman professes to sell his milk at cost price but he mixes it with water and thereby gains 10%. The percentage of water in the mixture is:
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A dishonest milkman professes to sell his milk at cost price but he mixes it with water and thereby gains 10%. The percentage of water in the mixture is-

Solution:
Let,
the cost price = 100
selling price = 110

So the amount of milk = 100/110
= 10/11

∴ Amount of water = (1 - 10/11) × 100%
= 9.09%

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ২) There are Tiger and peacock in zoo. The total number of their heads is 60 and the total number of their legs is 180. How many peacocks are there?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: There are Tiger and peacock in zoo. The total number of their heads is 60 and the total number of their legs is 180. How many peacocks are there?

Solution:
Let,
There are x peacocks

So the number of tiger = (60 - x)

ATQ,
2x + 4(60 - x) = 180
⇒ 2x + 240 - 4x = 180
⇒ 240 - 2x = 180
⇒ 240 - 180 = 2x
⇒ 60 = 2x
⇒ x = 60/2
∴ x = 30

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৩) A train running at the speed of 66 km/h crosses a pole in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A train running at the speed of 66 km/h crosses a pole in 15 seconds. What is the length of the train?

Solution:
Given,
Speed = 66 km/h
= (66 × 5/18) m/sec
= 55/3 m/sec

So the length of the train = (55/3 × 15) m
= 275 m

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৪) The speed of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 7. B takes 21 minutes less than A to reach a destination. Time in which B reach the destination?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: The speed of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 7. B takes 21 minutes less than A to reach a destination. Time in which B reach the destination?

Solution:
Given
The speed of A and B are in the ratio = 4 : 7

So the ratio of time taken = 7 : 4  [As Speed ∝ 1/Time, When distance remains constant.]

Let,
time taken by A and B be 7x and 4x minutes respectively.

ATQ,
7x - 4x = 21
⇒ 3x = 21
∴ x = 7

Hence, time taken by B = (4 × 7) minutes
= 28 minutes

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৫) A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 30 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A motorboat, whose speed in 15 km/h in still water goes 30 km downstream and comes back in a total of 4 hours 30 minutes. The speed of the stream (in km/h) is:

Solution:
Let,
The speed of the stream be x km/hr

Then,
Speed downstream = (15 + x) km/hr
Speed upstream = (15 - x) km/hr

∴ (30/15+x) + (30/15−x) = 4(1/2)
⇒ 900/(225 - x2) = 9/2
⇒ 2025 - 9x2 = 1800
⇒ 2025 - 1800 = 9x2
⇒ 9x2 = 225
⇒ x2 = 25
∴ x = 5 km/h

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৬) 800 grams of sugar solution has 40% sugar in it. How much sugar should be added to make 60% in the solution?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: 800 grams of sugar solution has 40% sugar in it. How much sugar should be added to make 60% in the solution? 

Solution:
Amount of sugar = 800 × 40/100
= 320 grams

Let,
x gm sugar to be added

ATQ,
(320 + x)/(800 + x) = 60%
⇒ (320 + x)/(800 + x) = 3/5
⇒ 1600 + 5x = 2400 + 3x
⇒ 5x - 3x = 2400 - 1600
⇒ 2x = 800
∴ x = 400

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৭) A man completes a certain journey by a car. If he covered 40% of the distance at the speed of 20kmph. 40% of the distance at 40km/h and the remaining of the distance at 10 kmph, his average speed is-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A man completes a certain journey by a car. If he covered 40% of the distance at the speed of 20kmph. 40% of the distance at 40km/h and the remaining of the distance at 10 kmph, his average speed is-

Solution:
Let,
The total distance be = 100 km.

Given,
40% of the distance at the speed of 20kmph
So the average time of first 40 km = 40/20 hours
= 2 hours

40% of the distance at the speed of 40kmph
So the average time of second 40 km = 40/40 hours
= 1 hours

the remaining 20 km of the distance at 10 kmph
So the average time of last 20 km = 20/10 hours
= 2 hours

Total time = (2 + 1 +2) hours
= 5 hours

Average speed = (total distance covered ÷ time taken)
= (100 ÷ 5) km/h
= 20 km/h

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৮) A train passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 15 seconds. If the speed of the train is 90 km/h, what is the length of the platform?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A train passes a station platform in 36 seconds and a man standing on the platform in 15 seconds. If the speed of the train is 90 km/h, what is the length of the platform?

Solution:
Given,
Speed of the train = 90 km/h
= (90 × 5/18) m/sec
= 25 m/sec

Length of the train = (25 x 15) m
= 375 m

Let,
The length of the platform = x metres.

ATQ,
(x + 375)/36 = 25
⇒ x + 375 = 900
⇒ x = 900 - 375
∴ x = 525 m

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ৯) A mixture contains 1/5 of element A and 4/5 of element B. When 5 ml of A is added to the mixture, the proportion of B in the mixture changes to 1/5. What amount of A was originally present in the mixture before the addition was made?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A mixture contains 1/5 of element A and 4/5 of element B. When 5 ml of A is added to the mixture, the proportion of B in the mixture changes to 1/5. What amount of A was originally present in the mixture before the addition was made?

Solution: 
Let,
Mixture be x ml.
A = x/5 ml
B = 4x/5 ml

After adding 5 ml of A to mixture, amount of B remained same.
And the mixure be x + 5 ml.
New
B = (x + 5)/5

Now,
(4x)/5 = (x + 5)/5
⇒ 20x = 5x + 25
⇒ 15x = 25
⇒ x = 25/15
∴ x = 5/3

Original amount of A = (5/3)/5 ml
= 1/3 ml

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১০) In a race of 200 meters, B can gives a start of 20 meters to A, and C can gives a start of 30 meters to B. The starts that C can gives to A, in the same race is-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: In a race of 200 meters, B can gives a start of 20 meters to A, and C can gives a start of 30 meters to B. The starts that C can gives to A, in the same race is-

Solution:
According to question,
When B runs 200 m meters, A runs 180 meters;
Hence, when B runs 170 meters,
A runs = (180 × 170)/200
= 153 meters

When C runs 200m, B runs 170 meters.
Hence,
C will give a start to A by = (200 - 153) meters
= 47 meters

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১১) A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 1 hour and goes 1 km along the current in 15 minutes. How long will it take to go 9 km in stationary water?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A boatman goes 2 km against the current of the stream in 1 hour and goes 1 km along the current in 15 minutes. How long will it take to go 9 km in stationary water?

Solution:
Rate downstream = (1/15 × 60) km/h
= 4 km/h

Rate upstream = 2 km/h

Speed in still water = (4 + 2)/2 km/h
= 3 km/h

Required time = (9/3) h
= 3 h

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১২) A 180 liter mixture of milk and water contains 30% water. How much milk, in liters must be added to the mixture will contain water and milk in the ratio of 1:7?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
সঠিক উত্তর: 252 liters
অপশনে সঠিক উত্তর না থাকায় প্রশ্নটি বাতিল করা হলো। 
-------------------------------- 

Question: A 180 liter mixture of milk and water contains 30% water. How much milk, in liters must be added to the mixture will contain water and milk in the ratio of 1:7?

Solution:
Milk = 180 × (100 -30)%
= 180 × 70%
= 180 × (70/100)
= 126

Remaining = 180 - 126 = 54 liters

Let,
x liter milk has to added

ATQ,
54 : (126 + x) = 1 : 7
⇒ 54/(126 + x) = 1/7
⇒ 378 = 126 + x
⇒ x = 378 - 126
∴ x = 252 liters

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৩) A man sitting in a train is counting the pillars of electricity. The distance between two pillars is 50 meters, and the speed of the train is 45 km/hr. In 4 hours, how many pillars will he count?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A man sitting in a train is counting the pillars of electricity. The distance between two pillars is 50 meters, and the speed of the train is 45 km/hr. In 4 hours, how many pillars will he count?

Solution:
Distance covered by the train in 4 hours = (Speed × Time)
= (45 × 4) km
= 180 km
= 180000 m

∴ Number of pillars counted by the man = (180000/50) + 1
= (3600 + 1)
= 3601

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৫) Two equal glasses are respectively two-third and three-fourth full of milk. They are then filled up with water and the contents are mixed in a tumbler. Ratio of milk and water in tumbler is
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: Two equal glasses are respectively two-third and three-fourth full of milk. They are then filled up with water and the contents are mixed in a tumbler. Ratio of milk and water in tumbler is 

Solution:
In 1st glass milk = 2/3
Water = (1 - 2/3)
= 1/3

In 2nd glass milk = 3/4
Water = (1 - 3/4)
= 1/4

Ratio of milk and water = (2/3 + 3/4) : (1/3 + 1/4)
= {(8 + 9)/12} : {(4 + 3)/12}
= (17/12) : (7/12)
= 17 : 7

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৬) A man can row at 8 kmph in still water. If the velocity of current is 2 kmph and it takes him 2 hour to row to a place and come back, how far is the place?
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A man can row at 8 kmph in still water. If the velocity of current is 2 kmph and it takes him 2 hour to row to a place and come back, how far is the place?

Solution:
Speed downstream = (8 + 2) kmph = 10 kmph
Speed upstream = (8 - 2) kmph = 6 kmph
Let the required distance be x km

ATQ,
(x/10) + (x/6) = 2
⇒ (3x + 5x)/30 = 2
⇒ 8x = 60
∴ x = 7.5

Solution:
Let Speed of the man is x kmph.

Let the speed of the man be x km/h
Distance covered by the man in 10 min = Distance covered by the bus in 5 min

According to the question
⇒ x × 10/60 = 30 × 5/60
⇒ 10x = 150 ⇒
x = 15 km/h

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ১৯) A merchant has 100 kg of sugar, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. The quantity sold at 18% profit is-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A merchant has 100 kg of sugar, part of which he sells at 8% profit and the rest at 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole. The quantity sold at 18% profit is-

Solution:
By the rule of alligation, we have:

⇒ Quantity of cheaper : Quantity of Dearer = (CP of of Dearer - Mean Price) : (Mean Price - CP of Cheaper)
⇒ Quantity of cheaper : Quantity of Dearer = (18-14) : (14-8)
= 4 : 6
= 2 : 3

∴ Quantity of 2nd kind = (3/5 × 100) kg
= 60 kg

Bank-Math-Master\t.question: ২০) A man covers half of his journey at 12 km/h and the remaining half at 6 km/h. His average speed is-
Bank-Math-Master\t.exp:
Question: A man covers half of his journey at 12 km/h and the remaining half at 6 km/h. His average speed is-

Solution:
Given,
Man covers half of his journey at 12 km/h
The remaining half at 6 km/h

His average speed is = (2 × 12 × 6)/(12 + 6)
= 144/18
= 8 km/h
